title: This Frog Freezes Solid Every Winter, Heart Stopped, Then Hops Away
subject: wood frog

scenes.text: This frog freezes solid every winter, and its heart stops beating.
Up to sixty-five percent of the water in its body turns to ice. No heartbeat, no breathing, for months.
So why doesn't it die? Its body floods with glucose, a natural antifreeze that keeps its cells from freezing.
In the coldest places, wood frogs in Alaska survive being frozen at about minus five degrees Fahrenheit.
In spring, the heart and brain thaw first, then the rest. Within about ten hours, the frog is moving again.
A frog that spends the winter frozen dead, and hops away alive.

description:
A wood frog freezes solid every winter and its heart stops, yet it thaws in spring and hops away.
Up to 65% of its body water turns to ice, and a glucose antifreeze protects its cells.
Could you survive being frozen for a winter?
first_comment: A frozen frog with no heartbeat comes back to life. What other animal record should we cover?
